text.0_Chapter, 0_Verse, 0_Comment: The burden. Our Sages disagreed about the identity of this prophet. According to all opinions, he prophesied after the Temple had been built, and he was the last of the prophets, as will be explained at the end of the book.
text.0_Chapter, 1_Verse, 0_Comment: I have loved you, because Hashem has an ancient love for Israel on account of His love for their forefathers. He therefore informed them that the essential love is His love for them in particular, without regard to that ancient love, which relates not to them but to their forefathers: I have loved you yourselves. And you say, “How have You loved us?” What proves that the love is directed toward us ourselves, and how, then, can it be known that it is not because of the ancient love for the forefathers? To this He replies: Was not Esau a brother to Jacob? Yet I loved Jacob. For if the love were only on account of the forefathers, Esau would also have a share in that love; why, then, does He love only Jacob? And lest they say that the love stems from both causes together—that He loves them for their own deeds, combined with the deeds of their forefathers and His love for them, in which case the love would still not relate to them alone but to them in conjunction with His love for their forefathers—to this He replies: “Was not…”
text.0_Chapter, 2_Verse, 0_Comment: But Esau I hated. Although it is conceivable that He would not love Esau because Esau lacked the love earned by his own deeds—and that the love of the forefathers alone would not suffice for God to love him unless it were joined by love for Esau himself—nevertheless, He should at least not hate Esau, since Esau possesses some claim to love through God’s love for his forefathers. It must therefore be that God’s love for Israel is based solely upon Israel’s own essential character. This nullifies, in Esau’s case, the ancestral love in which he shares and transforms it into hostility and hatred, since he did not make his deeds worthy. He proves that He hated Esau from the fact that I made his mountains desolate:
text.0_Chapter, 3_Verse, 0_Comment: For Edom may say, lest they argue that all this is no proof that it resulted from Hashem’s hatred of Esau, for it could be said that it was caused by the influence of the stars and his adverse fortune, or that it occurred by chance. This would prove only that He does not love Esau enough to exercise special Providence over him and avert the harm decreed by the stars, but it would not prove that He hates him and actively brings evil upon him. This is the meaning of For Edom may say, “We have become impoverished,”—this did not come from Hashem and His hatred, but we became impoverished through nature or fortune—“but we will return and rebuild the ruins,” when our fortune rises from its low state or when we regain strength through natural means. Thus says Hashem: He replies to them, “They may build, but I will tear down.” Although according to nature they ought to rebuild, I will tear down through Providence because of My hatred for them. And they shall be called—until they are called a people whose destruction has two causes: (1) because their land is the border of wickedness. In contrast to Hashem’s territory, which is the dwelling place of holiness and righteousness, where Hashem commanded the blessing, their territory is the dwelling place of wickedness and evil, the portion of Azazel, where ruin and desolation will always prevail; (2) because they are the people against whom Hashem is indignant forever, on account of their evil deeds.
text.0_Chapter, 4_Verse, 0_Comment: And your eyes shall see the vengeance that Hashem will exact from Edom, as in, “And you shall witness the recompense of the wicked.” And you shall say, “May Hashem be magnified beyond the border of Israel.” Just as wickedness will be brought low and its territory will become a desolate ruin, so will Hashem be magnified in His glory above the border of Israel; for when one rises, the other falls, as in the verse, “I shall be filled from the one that is laid waste.”
text.0_Chapter, 5_Verse, 0_Comment: A son. He means that a son honors his father and is careful to honor him because of the love with which he loves his father, while a servant honors his master out of fear, because his master rules over him and he fears his punishment; therefore, he will not do anything displeasing in his eyes. But if I am a Father—since you are like children before Me, serving out of love—where is My honor? And if I am a Master—since you do not possess the quality of love—then at least you ought to fear My punishment, since I am the Master of the entire world; where is the fear of Me? These two questions Hashem of Hosts addressed to you, the priests. He then explains the two questions. Regarding the first question, “If I am a Father, where is My honor?”—Hashem said to you, O priests who despise My name; and regarding the second question, “If I am a Master, where is the fear of Me?”—Hashem said it to you, the priests.
text.0_Chapter, 6_Verse, 0_Comment: You offer defiled bread upon My altar. That is, from the standpoint of the honor and love due to Hashem, it is improper for you to despise His name, for this is the opposite of honor; and from the standpoint of fear, it is improper for you to offer defiled bread, for you ought to fear punishment. Concerning these two accusations, He says, “And you say, ‘How have we despised Your name?’ And you say, ‘How have we defiled You?’”—for you deny these charges. He therefore demonstrates to them both that they despised His name and that they offered defiled bread. In response to “How have we despised Your name?” He answers: By saying, “The table of Hashem is contemptible.” You say that the sacrifice brought upon the table of Hashem—that is, upon the altar, as Ezekiel says, “This is the table that is before Hashem”—is something contemptible, because contemptible things, fat and blood, are offered upon it. By this you despise His name and His honor. And in response to the question “How have we defiled You?” he answers:
text.0_Chapter, 7_Verse, 0_Comment: When you offer a blind animal for sacrifice, is there nothing wrong with that? And even more, when you offer a lame or sick animal, whose blemish is more readily apparent than blindness, is there nothing wrong with that? By doing so, you offer defiled bread, since an animal with a blemish is unacceptable as a sacrifice. Present it, if you please, to your governor. If you were to present such a gift to the governor of Judah, who is merely flesh and blood, would he be pleased with you? Would he accept such a gift favorably? Or would he show you favor? Even if you were a person worthy of special consideration, he would no longer show you favor once his anger was kindled against you because of this insult.
text.0_Chapter, 8_Verse, 0_Comment: And now, if a human being would not accept such an offering, how can you imagine that you can entreat God’s favor with such an offering and that He will be gracious to us? This is a rhetorical question, corresponding to “Would he be pleased with you?” And corresponding to “Would he show you favor?” he explains: Since this has come from your hands—you priests have caused Him to become angry with you by bringing blemished animals before Him—how could He show favor to any of you?
text.0_Chapter, 9_Verse, 0_Comment: Who is there even among you who would shut the doors? He adds that, apart from the offering itself, you are also unworthy in your own right, and it would be fitting to shut the doors so that you could not enter My House. And if you do enter, it would be fitting that you not kindle a fire upon My altar in vain. Corresponding to “Who is there even among you who would shut the doors?” he explains: For I have no desire for you, and I do not want you to enter My House. Corresponding to “That you not kindle a fire upon My altar in vain,” he explains: And I will not accept an offering from your hand, even if it were not blemished. This also corresponds to the questions “Would he be pleased with you?” and “Would he show you favor?” Corresponding to “Would he show you favor?” and, as stated, “Would He show favor to any of you?” He says: “Who is there even among you?”—who thinks that I will show him favor because he is important in My eyes? Let him shut the doors and not enter My House, for I have no desire for you. And corresponding to “Would he be pleased with you?” He says: “Do not kindle a fire upon My altar,” for “I will not accept an offering from your hand.”
text.0_Chapter, 10_Verse, 0_Comment: For from the rising of the sun to its setting, although all the nations worship idols, nevertheless My name is great among the nations. For they all know that there is a First Cause exalted above all, whom they call “the God of gods.” They merely say that it is beneath His dignity to exercise Providence over lowly beings and that He has entrusted the governance of the lower world to His ministers—just as a king entrusts governance to his officers and servants and desires that honor be accorded to them because they have access to the king and serve as intermediaries between him and the people, so that their honor is the king’s honor. Likewise, everything they burn as incense to the stars and constellations is based upon their belief that these are close to the First Cause and receive their influence from Him. This is the meaning of and in every place incense is burned to one who is brought near to My name: whoever is brought near to My name is offered incense. That is, they burn sacrificial incense to whoever is brought near and is close to the name of Hashem; whoever they believe is brought near to Hashem’s name is offered incense. Thus, they burn incense to the host of heaven, which they regard as brought near and close to Hashem’s name. And they offer them a pure offering, clean and unblemished, rather than blemished, impure, or dishonorable things. This is because My name is great among the nations, so much so that they honor everyone brought near to His name and close to Him.
text.0_Chapter, 11_Verse, 0_Comment: But you profane it. You profane Hashem’s name by saying, “The table of Hashem is defiled.” Although you offer sacrifices to Him Himself, rather than to those brought near to His name, His table—the altar—is therefore itself brought near to His name, and you ought to honor it; yet you say that it is defiled. And its produce—its food—is contemptible. That is, Hashem’s table, namely the altar, has two aspects: (1) the things offered upon the altar to Hashem, such as the fat and blood of the sacrifices, concerning which you say that it is defiled; and (2) its fruit and produce—that is, the sacred meat eaten by the priests, such as the meat of the sin offering and the guilt offering, and that eaten by the owners, such as the meat of offerings of lesser sanctity, which they eat from the table of the Most High, as our Sages said, “The priests eat from the table of the Most High.” This is its produce—the produce and fruit of the table. Concerning this you say that its food is contemptible: you treat the eating of sacred meat with contempt, and it is despised in your eyes.
text.0_Chapter, 12_Verse, 0_Comment: And you say. Abarbanel explains that they would inflate the sacrificial animal, blowing air between its skin and flesh so that it would appear fat. When one carried it upon his shoulder, he would say, “Behold, what a burden!”—meaning, “It took me great toil and effort to carry it because of its tremendous weight.” But in truth, you inflated it, and it was filled with air. Apart from bringing a lean, inflated animal as a sacrifice, you also brought a stolen animal, making it a commandment fulfilled through a transgression, and a lame or sick animal, both of which are disqualified as sacrifices. And you brought the offering with it—the accompanying meal offering, which signifies that the sacrifice has been favorably accepted by Hashem as a pleasing aroma. Would I accept it from your hand, when the sacrificial animal itself is disqualified?
text.0_Chapter, 13_Verse, 0_Comment: And cursed is the deceiver—the cunning man who schemes to commit wickedness through his deceit—who has a male in his flock and therefore has no excuse that he possesses no other animal to sacrifice, yet vows and sacrifices a blemished animal to Hashem. He schemes wickedly in three respects: (1) He should have donated the male present in his flock by saying, “This animal is hereby an offering,” which is called a donation; instead, he makes a vow, saying, “I undertake to bring an offering,” and waits until the male is no longer in his flock. (2) He should have offered it as a burnt offering, which is consumed entirely upon the altar; instead, he sacrifices a peace offering, whose meat belongs to its owners. (3) At the very least, the sacrifice should be unblemished; instead, he brings a blemished animal. Therefore, this deceiver shall be cursed, for I am a great King, and the greater the King, the greater the punishment of one who profanes His honor; and My name is feared even among the nations. How, then, can any man among the children of Israel fail to fear Me?
text.1_Chapter, 0_Verse, 0_Comment: And now, this commandment is for you. I now command you to attend to this matter and to admonish the people concerning it.
text.1_Chapter, 1_Verse, 0_Comment: If you do not listen because I am warning you, and if you do not take it to heart through the prompting of reason, which itself requires this—to give honor to My name—then I will send the curse upon you. The curse of which I said, “Cursed is the deceiver,” I will send upon you. And I will curse your blessings—the blessings with which you bless the people in the Priestly Blessing after the offering of the sacrifice, concerning which it is said, “They shall place My name upon the children of Israel, and I will bless them,” meaning that through you Hashem will bless the people. But now that you remove My name from the children of Israel and profane it, I will transform your blessings into a curse. Indeed, I have already cursed it, because you do not take it to heart.
text.1_Chapter, 2_Verse, 0_Comment: Behold, I will rebuke the seed because of you. For they had been promised through Haggai (2:18–19) and Zechariah (chapter 8) that from the time they began building the Temple and offering sacrifices, blessing would rest upon the seed they sowed. But now, because you have not properly observed the requirements of the sacrificial service, I will rebuke the seed on your account so that it will not grow with blessing.
text.1_Chapter, 2_Verse, 1_Comment: And I will scatter dung upon your faces. Since the sacrifices are disqualified, nothing remains of them except the dung—the excrement and ashes of the animals offered—which you bring into the Temple; this I will scatter upon your faces. Likewise, I will scatter upon you the dung of the sacrifices that you offer on your festivals, and it shall carry you away with it: it will consume and burn you until you become like the dung and ashes.
text.1_Chapter, 3_Verse, 0_Comment: And you shall know that what I have sent to you—namely, this commandment—is because you have long been obligated by this commandment, so that My covenant might remain with Levi. For it was upon this condition that I made a covenant with Levi—that is, the covenant of the priesthood and the Levitical service—as he now explains.
text.1_Chapter, 4_Verse, 0_Comment: My covenant, which was with him, had two sides. On My side, it was a covenant of life and peace: through the covenant I promised him life and peace, as it is written, “Behold, I give him My covenant of peace,” and, “They shall keep your charge … so that neither they nor you shall die” (Numbers 18:3), and “You shall not profane the sacred things of the children of Israel, lest you die” (ibid. 18:32). His side of the covenant was: I gave them to him for reverence, and he revered Me—he was to revere Me with the awe of exaltation because of My greatness. In addition, he was terrified before My name—he trembled before Me with fear of punishment.
text.1_Chapter, 5_Verse, 0_Comment: Instruction. Through the fear of Hashem established in his heart, he will observe the words of Hashem, both in matters concerning teaching and testimony and in matters of conduct and practice. Concerning teaching, the teaching of truth was in his mouth: what he studied for himself was true teaching, in accordance with the wisdom received from Sinai; and injustice was not found on his lips: when he taught and rendered decisions for others, he ruled according to the law. I have explained elsewhere that the lips are external in relation to the mouth and signify what one expresses outwardly to teach others. I have further explained that the mouth always alludes to matters of wisdom, whereas the lips allude to matters of knowledge. That is, the mouth signifies what one has received from his teachers in matters of wisdom, which cannot be known independently but only through tradition. The verse says that he received a true tradition. The lips signify what he derives through his own understanding in matters accessible to reason, such as things apprehended through the senses or first principles that he knows independently with clear knowledge and expresses outwardly with his lips. In this there is a possibility of injustice if he errs in his reasoning and draws misleading inferences. It therefore says that injustice was not found on his lips. Concerning conduct governed by practical reason: in matters between man and God, he walked with Me in peace and uprightness; he did not deviate from Hashem’s commandments by disputing them, nor did he stray from the upright path and the commandments of the Torah. And in matters concerning others, he turned many away from sin through his rebukes and moral instruction. He now explains what the priest taught the people, both in Torah and in proper conduct.
text.1_Chapter, 6_Verse, 0_Comment: For the lips of a priest shall preserve knowledge: the teachings that he taught others with his lips were matters that he had investigated through his own reason. This falls under the category of knowledge, which denotes things that a person knows independently with clear understanding, and it is associated with the lips, as explained above. Thus, when the verse says, “For the lips of a priest,” it means that they preserved knowledge, so that everything accessible to reason would be known with clarity. This is contrasted with matters of wisdom received through tradition, for which there are no rational demonstrations and which are associated with the mouth.
text.1_Chapter, 6_Verse, 1_Comment: They shall seek Torah from his mouth, for he received both the Written and the Oral Torah, and those who receive the tradition from him shall seek it from him.
text.1_Chapter, 6_Verse, 2_Comment: For he is a messenger of Hashem of Hosts, for he is Hashem’s emissary and messenger: both to preserve within his heart the tradition and the Torah given at Sinai, and to safeguard sacred knowledge through the spirit of Hashem resting upon him.
text.1_Chapter, 7_Verse, 0_Comment: But you have been the opposite in both respects. In matters concerning your own conduct, you have departed from the path; and in matters concerning the guidance of the people and teaching them the statutes of the Torah, you have caused many to stumble through the Torah and through your rulings. Thus, you have forgotten the covenant of Levi, for it was concerning these two duties that I made a covenant with him.
text.1_Chapter, 8_Verse, 0_Comment: And I also. Therefore, corresponding to the honor in which the Levite had been held by the people, among whom he had been regarded as an exalted and holy messenger of Hashem—
text.1_Chapter, 8_Verse, 1_Comment: I have made you contemptible in the eyes of the people, and you are also truly debased before all the people. For you have fallen from your exalted position in proportion to the extent to which you do not keep My ways—as stated, “You have departed from the path”—and show partiality in applying the Torah—as stated, “You have caused many to stumble through the Torah.” To the extent that you continued to descend from the rank of the Levite and his priesthood, so did you descend into contempt and degradation.
text.1_Chapter, 9_Verse, 0_Comment: Have we not? After rebuking them concerning the sacrifices, he begins to rebuke them for marrying foreign women. They committed two wrongs in this regard: first, they married daughters of a foreign god; second, the foreign women were treated as mistresses, while their Israelite wives were regarded as maidservants in the eyes of those foreign women. When they married women from among their own people, the union was fitting in two respects: because of their familial kinship, since they were all descendants of the chosen forefathers; and because of their shared religion and faith, since both spouses believed in one God. They thereby united, became one flesh, and produced godly offspring like themselves. But when they married daughters of a foreign god, they impaired the unity of the family. Concerning this, he says, “Have we not all one father?” They also impaired the unity of faith, concerning which he says, “Has not one God created us?” That is, all of us, the children of Israel, are descendants of one father and believe in one God. This is not so of idolaters, who come from different families and believe in different gods. How, then, can you marry a daughter of a foreign god, thereby impairing the unity of the family? Concerning this, he says, “Why should a man betray his brother?” And concerning the unity of faith, he says, “Profaning the covenant of our forefathers,” who made a covenant with the one God.
text.1_Chapter, 10_Verse, 0_Comment: Judah has acted treacherously. This corresponds to the betrayal of the family.
text.1_Chapter, 10_Verse, 1_Comment: And an abomination has been committed in Israel. This refers to their having married idolatrous women, which, apart from being an act of treachery, was also an abomination. This occurred both in Israel and in Jerusalem, for there too they had foreign wives. He explains: For Judah has profaned that which is holy to Hashem, which He loved, and has married the daughter of a foreign god. There was treachery in loving her, and abomination in marrying the daughter of a foreign god.
text.1_Chapter, 11_Verse, 0_Comment: May Hashem cut off from the man who does this anyone who is awake or who answers. That is, no one will be found in his household who is awake from sleep, for they will all sleep the eternal sleep. Nor will there even be anyone dozing lightly enough to answer if called and roused from his sleep. As our Sages said, “What constitutes dozing? One who is asleep but not asleep, awake but not awake; when called, he answers.” This may refer either to the sleep of death or, as our Sages explained, to the slumber of the rational soul: “He shall have none awake among the sages or answering among the disciples.” The intellect of the sages is fully awake, while that of the disciples, although dozing, nevertheless answers and awakens when aroused. Likewise, if the man is a priest, there will be no one in his household who presents an offering to Hashem, for his children will follow their foreign mothers and will have a share neither in Torah nor in the Temple service.
text.1_Chapter, 12_Verse, 0_Comment: And this second thing you do. In addition to this, you commit another sin: the Hebrew women are oppressed under the authority of the foreign women, and they cover the altar with tears, weeping, and groaning, so that He can no longer turn toward your offering or accept it favorably from your hand. For before the altar they submit their case against you to the judgment of Heaven, as Solomon said in his prayer: “If a man sins against another, and an oath is imposed upon him … and the oath comes before Your altar, then You shall hear in heaven….”
text.1_Chapter, 13_Verse, 0_Comment: And you say, “Why?” Why is this sin so grave? He replies: Because Hashem has borne witness between you and the wife of your youth. Hashem is the witness between you. At the outset, Hashem witnessed the bond established between you when you betrothed her through the marriage canopy and kiddushin before Hashem; He testifies that it was done in His presence. And now He is the witness who warns you because you have betrayed her. You have violated the bond you formed with her, although she has not betrayed you: not through quarrels and disputes, for she is your companion; nor by committing adultery against her husband, for she is the wife of your covenant and has not violated the marital covenant.
text.1_Chapter, 14_Verse, 0_Comment: And did He not make one, with a remnant? He adduces proof of their sin from the creation of man. When Hashem created humanity, He did not create the male and female separately, as He created the other animals. Adam was initially created alone, and Eve was one of his ribs and was originally one body with him—as our Sages said, “They were created with two faces.” This is the meaning of “And did He not make one, with his flesh?” Hashem made the man one body together with his flesh—meaning his wife; the two were joined together when man was created.
text.1_Chapter, 14_Verse, 1_Comment: And He made a spirit for him. The man and the flesh joined to him shared one spirit. Thus, the two were created as one flesh and one spirit, unlike the other living creatures, which were created in pairs, separate both in body and in spirit. Why did He do this? Why did He not create the man and his wife immediately as separate beings? It was to teach that a man’s spouse must resemble him and be united with him: in flesh, by belonging to his people and ancestral house; and in spirit, by sharing the same religion and faith. This is the meaning of “Have we not all one father? Has not one God created us?”—just as the first man and his wife were originally one flesh and one spirit. This is the meaning of “And what does the one signify?” That is, what is the purpose of the oneness and unity that must exist between the spouses? He answers: He seeks godly offspring. Through their unity in flesh and spirit, the offspring born of this union will be godly offspring, not a mixed and incongruous offspring like that of animals, which do not preserve kinship and unity, but offspring like that of Adam, who begot a child in his likeness and image—the image of God. Therefore, guard yourselves in your spirit: restrain the appetitive spirit.
text.1_Chapter, 14_Verse, 2_Comment: And let no one betray the wife of his youth: let your spirit not betray the wife of your youth by hating her and loving another in her place, since the purpose of creation was that the two should share one spirit—a spirit of love and mutual affection.
text.1_Chapter, 15_Verse, 0_Comment: For if he hates her. If your spirit hates the woman, is displeased with her, and you cannot restrain your spirit from hating her, then send her away, says Hashem of Hosts. Did He not say in the Torah that if she finds no favor in his eyes, he must write her a bill of divorce and send her from his house?
text.1_Chapter, 15_Verse, 1_Comment: And it will cover the violence upon his garment. Sending her away will cover the violence upon his garment. That is, although this too is an act of violence, it is nevertheless covered and concealed violence. This is unlike keeping her in his house and treating her cruelly out of hatred, which is a very blatant act of violence. Better than either course, however, is that you guard yourselves in your spirit and do not act treacherously at all, so that you need never come to hatred and divorce.
text.1_Chapter, 16_Verse, 0_Comment: You have wearied Hashem with your words. After rebuking them for the wickedness of their deeds, he proceeds to rebuke them for the wickedness of their thoughts—their heretical and faithless ideas. He says: You attribute weariness to Hashem, as though fatigue and exhaustion existed before Him and He were incapable of exercising Providence over individual deeds and repaying each person according to his actions. He explains: By saying, “Everyone who does evil is good in the eyes of Hashem.” That is, you cite the prosperity of the wicked and the suffering of the righteous as proof that there is no Providence and no judgment or reckoning. For you say that one of two conclusions must necessarily be true: either there is Providence, but one who does evil is good in Hashem’s eyes, and therefore He does not punish the evildoer—
text.1_Chapter, 16_Verse, 1_Comment: Or, since that is false, the question arises: “Where is the God of justice?” Why does He not punish the evildoer in accordance with justice and righteousness? The phrase “And He delights in them” means: either evil is not evil at all but is good in Hashem’s eyes; or, if it is evil, He delights in evil and does not desire good at all; or else, where is the God of justice? Thus you question and argue. In the following passage, he proceeds to answer them.
text.2_Chapter, 0_Verse, 0_Comment: Behold, I send. He answers them: What you desire—that the God of justice reveal Himself, immediately punish the wicked, and reward the righteous—cannot occur in the present age. For the world is now still a realm of free choice and trial, and everything must proceed according to the way of nature so that people remain free to do good or evil and there remains room for trial, reward, and punishment. If the Holy One, blessed be He, were to reveal Himself in His glory, it would no longer be conceivable for anyone to commit an evil deed, since even for a minor sin he would be punished immediately and removed from the world, and all would fear to do evil. Therefore, this path—by which Hashem Himself will go forth to His creatures to judge them and govern them in this manner—has not yet been cleared or prepared in the present age. Only after the world has been perfected will “Behold, I send My messenger, and he shall clear this path before Me.” First, a prophet will go forth in Hashem’s name and clear this path of every stumbling block—that is, he will bring the world to repentance. Then, once the world has been perfected and the path prepared, “Hashem whom you seek will suddenly come to His Temple.” Hashem will then come to dwell in His Temple below and walk among you. At that time, “the messenger of the covenant whom you desire—behold,” he has come, for the messenger will arrive before Hashem, Hashem of Hosts. He is the messenger who will bring the world into the covenant of Torah and faith and into the covenant between humanity and God. Our Sages explained that this is Elijah, the messenger of the covenant, who will come first to turn many away from sin and who displayed zeal for the covenant at Shittim and in the days of Ahab.
text.2_Chapter, 1_Verse, 0_Comment: But who can endure? At that time, who will be able to endure even the day of His coming? Even before Hashem Himself appears, no one will be able to withstand the overwhelming fear produced merely by the arrival of that day. How much more so, who can stand when He appears? At the moment of His revelation, no creature will be able to stand. For He is like a refiner’s fire: He will remove all impurities, like fire that refines metals and removes their dross. He is also like the soap of launderers: just as launderers’ soap removes even the smallest stain from a garment and purifies it completely, so will He purify Israel. That is, the wicked, who resemble dross, He will remove by the fire that consumes them; and the righteous He will also cleanse, removing every stain from them until they are like a clean, pure, and whitened garment.
text.2_Chapter, 2_Verse, 0_Comment: And He shall sit as a refiner and purifier of silver. After refining away the dross—the wicked—which will occur immediately upon His appearance, He will then sit permanently and continue to refine and purify even the silver. That is, He will refine once more even the good people who remain after the dross and the wicked have been separated, like one who refines a second time pure silver from which the dross has already been removed and which is already properly called silver. As it is written, “Silver refined in a furnace upon the earth, purified seven times.” And He shall purify the sons of Levi: He will purify even the tribe of Levi, who resemble silver. And He shall refine them like gold and silver. This purification will resemble the refining of gold and silver: because gold is more precious, it requires greater refinement than silver, and greater care is taken to remove its impurities. Likewise, He will refine the sons of Aaron within the tribe of Levi more thoroughly than the other members of the tribe. And they shall be those who present an offering to Hashem in righteousness: the priests who serve Hashem by presenting offerings before Him will be only those who belonged to Hashem through righteousness—that is, through good deeds between man and God, which fall under the category of righteousness. As explained in Ezekiel, chapter 43, only the priests descended from Zadok will be fit to offer sacrifices in the future Temple. The other priests who did not remain steadfast in their righteousness will not approach the altar to offer a sacrifice to Hashem.
text.2_Chapter, 3_Verse, 0_Comment: And it shall be pleasing to Hashem. Then the offering of Judah shall be pleasing as in the days of old. Our Sages explained “as in the days of old” to mean the days of Moses, and “as in former years” to mean the days of Solomon, when fire descended from heaven and consumed the burnt offering; so shall it be in the future. Another interpretation: “As in the days of old” means the days of Noah, and “as in former years” means the days of Abel, when idolatry did not yet exist. That is, idolatry will likewise cease to exist in those days, and Hashem will be One and His name One.
text.2_Chapter, 4_Verse, 0_Comment: And I will draw near. That is, what you seek—that Hashem be present among human beings in this age to judge the righteous and the wicked and immediately dispense their rewards and punishments—cannot occur until the future time of the world’s perfection. Then, not even the slightest form of sin will be found, for Hashem will enter into judgment by fire. The present age, however, is a world of free choice, change, and trial, and therefore cannot be governed in this manner. Nevertheless, although I conduct Myself toward idolaters through concealment, allowing the world to follow its natural course and the wicked to prosper until the appointed end, when I will sit in judgment over all the nations, I will draw near to you for judgment even before that future time. Therefore, He says, “And I will draw near,” indicating that He will come before the distant appointed time. This means that His judgments upon Israel will not remain as distant from them as they are from the idolatrous nations. Although this judgment will not be like that of the future age, when He will refine away even the slightest impurity and minor sin, nevertheless, I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers and the adulterers and those who commit other grave transgressions. Against these I will be a swift witness even before that distant future time. This is because I cannot refrain from punishing you until your measure of sin is full, for you would then be utterly destroyed. This is the meaning of what follows:
text.2_Chapter, 5_Verse, 0_Comment: For I, Hashem, have not changed My word or My promise at any time. I promised the forefathers that I would not destroy you; and because I have not changed My promise, you, the children of Jacob, have not been consumed. I am therefore compelled to exact punishment from you for your sins immediately, before your measure of sin becomes full, at which point you would deserve total destruction. But regarding the idolatrous nations, whom I did not promise that I would not destroy, I wait until their measure is full, and then they are utterly destroyed. Our Sages similarly interpreted this verse in the first chapter of Sotah, teaching that the Holy One, blessed be He, exacts punishment from Israel little by little. They cite this verse as proof: “I, Hashem, have not changed”—I have never struck a nation and then struck it a second time, for it is destroyed by the first blow; “but you, the children of Jacob, have not been consumed.” They thus explained that He punishes Israel immediately so that they will not be destroyed when their measure of sin becomes full.
text.2_Chapter, 6_Verse, 0_Comment: From the days. He begins to rebuke them for failing to separate the priestly gifts and tithes. He says: From the days of your forefathers, you have departed from My statutes, for they too were not careful about the priestly gifts and tithes. I therefore warn you: Return to Me, and I will return to you. Because of the sin of neglecting the priestly gifts and tithes, the rains are withheld, for the laws of heaven depend upon these statutes. When you departed from the statutes of the priestly gifts and tithes, I removed the laws governing rain and produce; but if you return to Me, I will return to bestow rain and blessing.
text.2_Chapter, 7_Verse, 0_Comment: Will a man rob? Is it proper for a person to rob God by withholding what is due to Him? And when you say, “How have we robbed You?”—it is through the tithes and the priestly gifts, which are Hashem’s portion.
text.2_Chapter, 8_Verse, 0_Comment: With a curse. In particular, you gain nothing from this theft, for through it you are cursed with a curse; nevertheless, you continue to rob Me. And the whole nation does this, not merely a few individuals.
text.2_Chapter, 9_Verse, 0_Comment: Bring. He explains the meaning of “Return to Me, and I will return to you”: Bring the entire tithe into the storehouse, so that there may be sustenance in My House for the Levites who guard the Temple and the priests who serve in the House of Hashem. They are like members of Hashem’s household, whose sustenance is His responsibility. And test Me, if you please, in this. Although it is forbidden to test Hashem, as it is written, “You shall not test Hashem,” this is permitted, because it is not a test but an examination. There is a distinction between testing and examining: one who tests something seeks to discover whether it possesses a capacity beyond what has previously been known of it—for example, testing whether gold has the power of magnetic attraction. One who examines something, however, determines whether it conforms to its ordinary nature—for example, examining gold to see whether it is free of impurities. If the blessing were produced through nature and the influence of the stars, this would constitute a test, since nature cannot provide more than its natural limits allow. But I promise: I will open for you the windows of heaven and pour out blessing for you beyond the limits of nature. The blessing will continue until there is no limit, for a blessing that comes through the natural heavens necessarily has a boundary, and upon reaching that boundary one must say, “Enough.” But Hashem’s blessing, which comes miraculously, has no boundary and will never be told, “Enough,” for it will continue increasing without end. This is therefore not a test but an examination, since the blessing comes from Hashem’s treasury, where it does not exceed His power. Moreover, because He has already promised the blessing, this merely examines whether He will fulfill His word. Thus, our Sages related that Reish Lakish heard a child say, “Tithe so that you may become wealthy.” He asked him, “Is it permissible to test God?” The child answered, “In this manner it is permissible, as it is written, ‘Test Me, if you please, in this.’” The child meant that this does not fall within the category of the forbidden testing of Hashem; it is merely an examination, and no prohibition was given against examination.
text.2_Chapter, 10_Verse, 0_Comment: And I will rebuke. For your sake, I will also rebuke the locust that devours the produce, so that it will not destroy the fruit of the soil; likewise, the vine will not miscarry its fruit.
text.2_Chapter, 11_Verse, 0_Comment: And they shall call you fortunate. Consequently, all the nations will consider you fortunate when they see that yours is the land in which Hashem delights, which He blesses and over which He exercises His Providence.
text.2_Chapter, 12_Verse, 0_Comment: They have been strong. After initially mentioning their question concerning the prosperity of the wicked, from which they sought to prove that there is no Providence or justice—as stated, “Everyone who does evil is good in the eyes of Hashem,” or, “Where is the God of justice?”—and after giving them the answer to this question, He says that your words have still been strong against Me. You have not accepted the preceding answer, but persist in arguing against Me and attempting to refute My words, for—
text.2_Chapter, 13_Verse, 0_Comment: You have said. That is, they reply that although the preceding answer resolves the difficulty posed by the prosperity of the wicked, the suffering of righteous people who have not sinned yet live lives of misery still remains unexplained. Therefore, you have said, “It is futile to serve God.” This means that such service provides no benefit, either to the One served or to the one who serves. It does not benefit the One served, for one cannot say that Hashem desires this service because He needs it; that would be a futile and meaningless claim, since Hashem has no need of our service: “If you are righteous, what do you give Him?” Concerning this they say, “It is futile to serve God.” Nor does it benefit the servant, for one might say that Hashem commanded this service not for His own need but so that the servant might receive a reward for it. Concerning this they say, “What profit is there in our having kept His charge?” We have gained nothing from it, for we have walked mournfully before Hashem of Hosts. We have labored in vain in our service and have received no reward whatsoever; on the contrary—
text.2_Chapter, 14_Verse, 0_Comment: And now we call the arrogant fortunate. They do not labor to serve Hashem, yet those who practice wickedness have also prospered and have lost nothing. They have even tested God to see whether He could punish them, yet they escaped, for no harm whatsoever befell them.
text.2_Chapter, 15_Verse, 0_Comment: Then. That is, the true God-fearing people, who do not serve in order to receive a reward, also discussed these matters with one another. From them they concluded that this world is not the world of reward and punishment, but the world of trial. The very fact that the righteous suffer in this world elevates their service to a higher level: they serve neither from fear of punishment nor in expectation of reward, but from exalted reverence for Hashem, since they do not expect to be rewarded in this world for their service. This is pleasing in the eyes of Hashem, who knows all hidden things. And Hashem attended and heard, and a book of remembrance was written before Him. Although He did not reward them in this world for their good deeds, He recorded their deeds in the special book kept before Him as a remembrance for those who fear Hashem and contemplate His name. For the very fact that they remained steadfast in their faith despite the many evils and troubles that befell them demonstrates that they truly fear Hashem. Their fear is not self-directed fear—that is, fear of punishment—but fear of Hashem, the awe of His exaltedness. They do not serve with reward or recompense in mind, but only to sanctify His unique name. They serve without intending to receive a reward, and at that time they were inscribed in this book as a remembrance.
text.2_Chapter, 16_Verse, 0_Comment: And they shall be Mine, says Hashem, as a treasure for the day that I prepare. The order of the words is: “And they shall be My treasure for the day that I prepare.” Hashem stores up for them a treasure—a precious store reserved for that day. Just as they served Him out of love, so shall they be a treasured possession to Hashem and receive a precious, treasured reward. And I will have compassion upon them, as a man has compassion upon his son who serves him. A servant or laborer who works for wages is paid immediately; but a son who serves his father out of love is not paid at once. Instead, his father prepares a lasting treasure for him, one that will endure for generations and never be lost. Likewise, those who serve out of love, without expectation of reward, are not rewarded in this world, which is transitory and in which their reward would also pass away. Rather, He stores up their reward to give them in the future, in the eternal world, where their reward will be great, everlasting, and without limit.
text.2_Chapter, 17_Verse, 0_Comment: And you shall return. At that time, you will return to this world by rising in the resurrection of the dead, and you shall see the difference between the righteous and the wicked. You will also see a distinction among the righteous themselves: between one who serves God and one who does not serve Him. That is, between one who serves out of love, whose ultimate purpose is to serve God, and one who serves in expectation of reward or from fear of punishment. The latter does not serve as a true servant should—without regard for receiving a reward—for this is the manner of a hired laborer, not a servant. When one serves in order to receive a reward, the primary purpose of the service is his own benefit, rather than the service of God. Thus, our Sages said in tractate Hagigah: “Is not ‘the righteous’ identical with ‘one who serves God’? Rather, both ‘one who serves Him’ and ‘one who does not serve Him’ are completely righteous. Yet one who reviews his lesson one hundred times cannot be compared to one who reviews it one hundred and one times.”
text.2_Chapter, 18_Verse, 0_Comment: For behold, the day is coming. He depicts the Day of Judgment, when the fire of punishment will burn like the fire of a furnace. Because of their wickedness, the wicked are destined to be consumed by this fire like straw, and the day will set them ablaze until neither root nor branch remains of them.
text.2_Chapter, 19_Verse, 0_Comment: And it shall shine. But for you who fear My name—the righteous who served out of love—righteousness, meaning the good deeds they performed, will be like a shining sun. Therefore, He calls it “the sun of righteousness.” This sun will bring healing in its wings from the burning heat. The image is that the Divine light will be revealed in both of its aspects, for light contains both illumination and fire: it will reveal its illumination to the righteous and its fire to the wicked, as it is written, “The light of Israel shall become a fire,” as I explained there.
text.2_Chapter, 19_Verse, 1_Comment: And you shall go forth and spread out like calves of the stall—the calves brought in to thresh the grain, which eat while treading it beneath their feet. He now explains what they will thresh:
text.2_Chapter, 20_Verse, 0_Comment: And you shall trample the wicked. They will tread the wicked beneath their feet until they become like a crushed mass, for they will be like ashes beneath the soles of your feet. The burning heat will consume them and reduce them to ashes, and you will tread upon those ashes until they become a compacted mass.
text.2_Chapter, 21_Verse, 0_Comment: Remember the Torah of Moses. With these words the prophet concluded his message. This was the final prophecy, after which no prophet or seer would prophesy again until the time of the End. He therefore informed them that from then onward they should no longer expect to receive the word of Hashem through prophecy. Instead, they must remember the Torah of Moses, observe everything written in it, and allow it to instruct them in what they should do.
text.2_Chapter, 22_Verse, 0_Comment: Behold. Before the coming of the great day, prophecy will return to you through the greatest of the prophets, Elijah the prophet, who will then reveal himself.
text.2_Chapter, 23_Verse, 0_Comment: And he shall turn. He will bring the entire world to repentance. He will turn the hearts of the children who have been led away from the Torah of their forefathers back toward their fathers, so that they return to the religion and Torah of their ancestors; and through this, he will turn the hearts of the fathers toward their children. He explains why Elijah will be sent in advance at that time to set the people upon the proper path: lest I come suddenly and strike the entire land with utter destruction. He will therefore first send the messenger of the covenant to bring them to repentance and prepare them before Hashem comes to judge the earth; then sovereignty shall belong to Hashem.
